ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, it is known that the parabola $y=x^{2}+bx$ passes through point $A(2,0)$ and point $B(-1, m)$, with its vertex at point $D$. What is the value of $\tan(\angle ABD)$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect BD and AD, 

\[
\because y=x^{2}-2x=(x-1)^{2}-1,
\]

\[
\therefore \text{the coordinates of point } D \text{ are } D(1, -1),
\]

\[
\because A(2,0), B(-1, 3),
\]

\[
\therefore AB^{2}=(-1-2)^{2}+3^{2}=18, AD^{2}=(2-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}=2, BD^{2}=(-1-1)^{2}+(-1-3)^{2}=20,
\]

\[
\therefore AB^{2}+AD^{2}=BD^{2},
\]

\[
\therefore \triangle ABD \text{ is a right-angled triangle},
\]

\[
\therefore \tan\angle ABD=\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{18}}=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}
\]
